evidence.method: transform restated from the source COGs' geotransform, which the store's regular 1-D coordinates agree with; CRS restated from the source grid mapping (latitude_longitude) and the datum its user guide states
evidence.crs_from: the 2127 source COGs (https://projects.pawsey.org.au/aad-derived/esacci-oc/v6.0-release/geographic/5day/chlor_a_log10_bias/<year>/*.tif) declare EPSG:4326 (WGS 84), origin -180, 90, cell 0.041666666666666664 degrees, 4320 x 8640, AREA_OR_POINT=Area (gdal.Open on each COG, GDAL 3.13.3, PROJ 9.9.0, 2026-11-28). py/esacci_cog.py writes EPSG:4326 and the geotransform (-180, 1/24, 0, 90, 0, -1/24) into each COG, after checking the netCDF lat and lon against it to 1e-6 degree. The netCDF files (https://www.oceancolour.org/thredds/fileServer/cci/v6.0-release/geographic/<cadence>/chlor_a/<year>/) hold a CF grid mapping variable crs with grid_mapping_name latitude_longitude and no datum or ellipsoid parameters, and no data variable names it in a grid_mapping attribute (OPeNDAP DAS of the 1997-09 and 2026-09 monthly and the 2026-09-18 5-day files, 2026-11-28). The Product User Guide for v6.0 Dataset (ESA OC-CCI, D4.2, issue 6.5, 2024-04-11), section 7.4: "All latitudes and longitudes are given in WGS/84 datum"; section 7.5 shows chlor_a:grid_mapping = "crs", which the served files do not carry
evidence.note: the published store's coordinates (built 2026-11-03) were written with 10 significant digits (0.04166666667 for 1/24) and restate the corner 8e-07 of a cell from the COG's; py/plan_cog.py writes 17 from 2026-11-28; overview levels (<array>_x<f>, byterefs decision 0006) have no documents of their own: py/assertions.py applies this assertion scaled to each level
